messages.author: 27557a5f7104d6a9
messages.subject: More efficient vectorization?
parts:
Say that I have some counts data generated like so in R:

N <- 10000
L <- 5
df <- data.frame(C= rpois(N, L))

I want to estimate L with this Stan code:

data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=0> C[N];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> L;
}
model {
  C ~ poisson(L);
}

But it sometimes arises that I have data similar to df above, but in tabulated form, where each unique count value is listed and it's noted how often it appears. For example, again in R:

library("tidyverse")
df.tab <- df %>% group_by(C) %>% summarize(num = n())

To estimate L I would treat it with this Stan code:

data {
  int<lower=0> N;
  int<lower=0> num[N];
  int<lower=0> C[N];
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0> L;
}
model {
  for (i in 1:N) { for (j in 1:num[i]) { C[i] ~ poisson(L); }; }
}

 I believe this second model is correct, but is there a better way to vectorize it?

messages.author: bcfb6bc9f75aae0f
messages.subject: Re: More efficient vectorization?
parts:
target += num[i]*poisson_lpmf(C[i] | L);
  }
}

(And you should specify a prior for L...).

HTH,

--
Emmanuel Charpentier
